title: Marguerite and the Horizon
premise: Ivo Zhou, a xenolinguist exiled to a forgotten beacon station after his translations helped justify a colonial atrocity, receives a distress call in Ashkari — a language he alone can still read, extinct since the war he enabled. The signal comes from survivors of an Ashkari seed-ship hiding in dead space, and the only relay that can answer them sits beyond a decaying reactor on a countdown Ivo cannot stop. Racing the signal's fading window, Ivo joins a ragged salvage crew who become the family he never believed he deserved, and together they reach the relay just as the reactor fails. In the end, Ivo broadcasts the survivors' location against orders, choosing belonging and restitution over the safety of silence — and finally dreams again, this time in two languages.
about_author: Rosalind Sterling is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction. She writes about language, loneliness, and the signals people send when they believe no one is left to hear them.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes his isolated routine maintaining the beacon, his fractured relationship with human language, and the guilt that drove him into exile. He translates maintenance logs aloud just to hear a voice. Emotional beat: quiet despair disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Language Out of Time
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The beacon intercepts a distress signal in Ashkari — grammatically alive, unmistakably recent. Ivo verifies it three times through the night, hands shaking. Emotional beat: terror and longing colliding; the dead speaking again.

chapters.title: What I Broke
chapters.summary: Flashback interlude, Ivo's POV. Reveals how his wartime translations were weaponized to locate Ashkari settlements, and why he stopped dreaming in any language at all. Emotional beat: shame as the engine of exile.

chapters.title: The Salvage Crew of the Kestrel
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He sends a desperate reply and hires passage with a small salvage crew: brusque captain Odile Ferro, engineer Tam, and medic Junie. They think he's chasing salvage rights; he lets them. Emotional beat: guarded first contact between strangers.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. En route, they learn the relay's reactor has begun an irreversible shutdown sequence — roughly forty days of power left. The distress signal will decay below detectability long before rescue could arrive conventionally. Emotional beat: the clock starts; hope acquires a deadline.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Dying
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo decoding the signal's shifting tenses, and Odile watching him work. The message reveals survivors aboard a drifting seed-ship, children among them, rationing air. Emotional beat: Ivo realizes the signal is not only asking for help — it's saying goodbye.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The Kestrel crosses into the navigation-dead zone where no charts exist. A micrometeorite storm cripples their long-range antenna. Emotional beat: the crew's found-family bonds begin forming under pressure, with Junie quietly adopting Ivo.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Words
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers Ivo's identity from an old bounty notice and confronts him privately. Instead of exposing him, Tam demands Ivo teach her fragments of Ashkari — she lost her own heritage language as a child. Emotional beat: betrayal deferred into unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Days
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fuel calculations show they can reach the relay or turn back — not both. Odile, haunted by a crew she once abandoned, chooses to press on over Tam's objection. Emotional beat: leadership as an act of faith; corruption of self-preservation resisted.

chapters.title: Voices in the Static
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He begins answering the signal directly, teaching the survivors his voice so they'll trust whoever comes. A child named Sefa answers back, asking if he dreams. Emotional beat: tenderness piercing guilt; Ivo lies and says yes.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. They arrive to find the relay half-consumed by a rogue mining consortium already stripping it for parts, its reactor countdown accelerated by their scavenging. Emotional beat: rage at power devouring even memory; the race becomes a confrontation.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Consortium director Hale Voss offers the crew triple pay to walk away and let the relay die quietly — the survivors' existence embarrasses the government that exterminated them. Junie refuses first. Emotional beat: the theme of corruption made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sabotaged systems force manual translation routing; Ivo works without sleep, and the boundary between languages dissolves — he begins dreaming in Ashkari for the first time in years. Emotional beat: healing and breakdown arriving together.

chapters.title: What Voss Keeps
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie infiltrates the consortium habitat and finds Voss hoarding recovered Ashkari cultural archives — selling extinction as collectibles. She steals a data core containing the seed-ship's original flight plan. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small Hours
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Voss, refused, seizes the Kestrel and maroons the crew on the relay ring. Tam's engineering knowledge becomes their lifeline; she and Odile reconcile in the dark. Emotional beat: lowest point — but the found family holds.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. From a jury-rigged console, Ivo re-establishes contact with Sefa and learns the seed-ship still has maneuvering fuel — enough to reach the relay themselves if someone guides them through dead space. Emotional beat: agency returns; the hunted become navigators.

chapters.title: The Long Answer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew retakes the Kestrel in a near-silent boarding action, using Ivo's Ashkari to coordinate with the seed-ship's adult survivors acting as inside eyes. Emotional beat: competence and courage; guilt transmuted into action.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Guiding the seed-ship through the dead zone by relayed signal, Ivo makes a critical translation error under exhaustion; a course correction nearly kills them. Sefa talks him back from collapse. Emotional beat: fallibility forgiven; the child steadies the man.

chapters.title: Zero Day
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The seed-ship docks as the reactor hits final countdown; Voss attempts one last seizure of the survivors' ship as salvage. The crew and survivors hold the docking ring together. Emotional beat: climax — every theme collides at the airlock.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With minutes of power left, Ivo must choose: transmit the survivors' verified location to open space, defying the government blackout that would keep them hidden and deniable, or stay silent and safe. He transmits. Emotional beat: the moral climax; restitution spoken aloud.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Aftermath: the broadcast forces official recognition; Voss is investigated; the Kestrel crew is offered amnesty and refuses it, choosing each other instead. The survivors begin rebuilding aboard a station offered by an independent colony. Emotional beat: consequences land; belonging chosen over absolution.

chapters.title: Two Languages
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, coda. Ivo stays on as the settlement's linguist, teaching Ashkari to children like Sefa and learning to be taught in return. On the last page, he falls asleep mid-sentence and dreams — fluently, peacefully, in both tongues. Emotional beat: resolution; the horizon finally arrives.
